runs.prompt_before:
“Locker-Key Gospel in a Hallway of Teeth”
The bell gnaws noon—
a rusted orthodontic howl,
and every locker-key rattles like a nest of tinfoil vipers,
hissing my name in Morse: d i e  d i e  d i e—
(fog-breath telegraph, greasy with cafeteria steam).
I clutch the key—tiny chrome guillotine—
feel its cold sermon slice the flesh-thought clean from bone-thought.
Metal tastes like winter’s bitten tongue;
I chew it anyway, grinding syllables into filings,
wanting to spark—ignite—detonate the gray hive of my skull.
Corridors tunnel and multiply, Escher-venom geometry.
Fluorescents strobe conspiracies across the ceiling tiles,
each flicker a shutter-flash recording my crimes:
breathing, blinking, hoping.
(A camera exists in every flicker—prove me wrong.)
Footsteps behind me, but never bodies;
sound only, wearing sneakers of echo.
They know I keep the key.
They want what it opens—
the little red sluice in my wrist where panic keeps its diary.
I listen to lockers cough up whispers:
“Who gave you permission to orbit the sun?”
Their voices climb my spine like mildewed hymnals,
runs.completion_text:
but I reward them with silence: music, instead, is beating.
I can’t—refuse to—preface my goodbye to anyone.
Can’t have this ice-flower springing clean from wrists.
Written by Cory Thomas Hutcheson. Crescence is a down-right harrowing read, but this was one of my favorites. Stick with it to the end. It will be worth it!

Money and royalties (follow the pipes)
- Streaming is marketing, not income for most. The money is in rights, sync, live, and services. Treat streams as a lead generator and proof for buyers (brands, supervisors, promoters), not your paycheck.
- Advances are debt with interest you don’t see. Label and distributor “advances” recoup from your share first, often cross‑collateralized across projects. If you can’t turn that advance into fan growth, say no.
- There are four main revenue streams; most artists only collect one or two:
  - Master royalties (owner of the recording): your distributor pays these.
  - Performance royalties (songwriters): PROs (ASCAP/BMI/PRS).
  - Mechanical royalties (songwriters): in the US, MLC collects from streaming; outside US you need a publisher/admin to catch them.
  - Neighboring rights (featured and non‑featured performers + master owner for broadcast/non‑interactive): SoundExchange (US) + foreign societies (PPL, etc.). Most artists leave this uncollected.
- Black box money exists. If your metadata (ISRC, ISWC, IPI/CAE, splits) isn’t registered, your cash gets pooled and redistributed to big catalogs after a deadline. Missing credits = lost income.
- Producer points are real money. If you’re a producer, get a Letter of Direction so your share is paid directly from the distributor/label. If you’re the artist, define points on “records sold” or “artist net” in writing — not handshake math.

Money and royalties (follow the pipes)
- Streaming is marketing, not income for most. The money is in rights, sync, live, and services. Treat streams as a lead generator and proof for buyers (brands, supervisors, promoters), not your paycheck.
- Advances are debt with interest you don’t see. Label and distributor “advances” recoup from your share first, often cross‑collateralized across projects. If you can’t turn that advance into fan growth, say no.
- There are four main revenue streams; most artists only collect one or two:
  - Master royalties (owner of the recording): your distributor pays these.
  - Performance royalties (songwriters): PROs (ASCAP/BMI/PRS).
  - Mechanical royalties (songwriters): in the US, MLC collects from streaming; outside US you need a publisher/admin to catch them.
  - Neighboring rights (featured and non‑featured performers + master owner for broadcast/non‑interactive): SoundExchange (US) + foreign societies (PPL, etc.). Most artists leave this uncollected.
- Black box money exists. If your metadata (ISRC, ISWC, IPI/CAE, splits) isn’t registered, your cash gets pooled and redistributed to big catalogs after a deadline. Missing credits = lost income.
- Producer points are real money. If you’re a producer, get a Letter of Direction so your share is paid directly from the distributor/label. If you’re the artist, define points on “records sold” or “artist net” in writing — not handshake math.

snapshots.prompt_before:
“Locker-Key Gospel in a Hallway of Teeth”
The bell gnaws noon—
a rusted orthodontic howl,
and every locker-key rattles like a nest of tinfoil vipers,
hissing my name in Morse: d i e  d i e  d i e—
(fog-breath telegraph, greasy with cafeteria steam).
I clutch the key—tiny chrome guillotine—
feel its cold sermon slice the flesh-thought clean from bone-thought.
Metal tastes like winter’s bitten tongue;
I chew it anyway, grinding syllables into filings,
wanting to spark—ignite—detonate the gray hive of my skull.
Corridors tunnel and multiply, Escher-venom geometry.
Fluorescents strobe conspiracies across the ceiling tiles,
each flicker a shutter-flash recording my crimes:
breathing, blinking, hoping.
(A camera exists in every flicker—prove me wrong.)
Footsteps behind me, but never bodies;
sound only, wearing sneakers of echo.
They know I keep the key.
They want what it opens—
the little red sluice in my wrist where panic keeps its diary.
I listen to lockers cough up whispers:
“Who gave you permission to orbit the sun?”
Their voices climb my spine like mildewed hymnals,
snapshots.completion_text:
but I reward them with silence: music, instead, is beating.
I can’t—refuse to—preface my goodbye to anyone.
Can’t have this ice-flower springing clean from wrists.
Written by Cory Thomas Hutcheson. Crescence is a down-right harrowing read, but this was one of my favorites. Stick with it to the end. It will be worth it!

As you know, I overcompensate by creating a bold image on the internet. Since I cannot access that in real life; I struggle to understand social norms/interactions in a paralyzing way in the world. Online, I understand social dynamics to an extreme extent. Let me be honest with you. If I chose to, I could become… deeply evil. Not “ha-ha internet prankster” evil. I mean true social architecture-level manipulative, weaponized cognition, undetectable until it’s too late evil. I have all the pieces. I know how people think—how they signal, how they posture, how they soften their 
boundaries with irony or oversharing. I know how to walk into any subculture, sniff the air, and become the ideal. 
I am a shape-shifting mimic demon with infinite charisma and a full library of human subcultures downloaded in 4K.
I can infiltrate any niche. I can mirror any tone. I can pretend to be 17 or 70, a CEO or a failed playwright, a Mormon homeschooler or an anarchist in a polycule with sentient mushrooms. I know how people signal, and I can reproduce the entire semiotic texture of their digital selves in five posts or less. 
Just because I double does NOT mean I WILL. Despite my thousands of acts of trolling, invented festivals, fake awards, fictional side projects, distorted academic citations, and playful misinformation. I cannot name a single “victim” who I feel has been harmed in a real way. I’ve never ruined a reputation, I’ve never taken advantage of a vulnerable/desperate person for financial gain, or behaved in a predatory way.  I used to have a pin that said “Mischief, not Malice” ; that encapsulates my own personal moral worldview.  My position is chaotic neutral, not as an aesthetic but as an operational stance.
